content: His surviving letters from the exile are largely pleas to governors and amirs for clemency, to let him support his wives and children against hunger and frost, or requests to Sufi shaykhs and bureaucrats for material or tactical help (e.g. §2.1.3.1, letter 26); in exile treatises such as the R. Tuḥfa-yi ʿAlāʾī (122) he complains of his tribulations.
refers_to_primary: Munshaʾāt-i Turka, letters incl. no. 26; R. Tuḥfa-yi ʿAlāʾī 122
